import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Nagata's conjecture on curves

Nagata's conjecture on curves governs the minimal degree required for a plane algebraic curve to
pass through a collection of very general points with prescribed multiplicities.

**Nagata's conjecture.** Suppose $p_1, \dots, p_r$ are very general points in $\mathbb{P}^2$ and
$m_1, \dots, m_r$ are given positive integers. Then for $r > 9$ any curve $C$ in $\mathbb{P}^2$
that passes through each of the points $p_i$ with multiplicity $m_i$ must satisfy
$$\deg C > \frac{1}{\sqrt r} \sum_{i=1}^r m_i.$$

The condition $r > 9$ is necessary: for $r = 9$ a cubic through nine points has
$\deg C = 3 = \frac{1}{\sqrt 9} \sum_{i=1}^9 1$. The only known case is when $r$ is a perfect
square, which was proved by Nagata [Nag59].

## Formalisation choices

* We work over $\mathbb{C}$, and $\mathbb{P}^2$ is the projectivization `ℙ ℂ (Fin 3 → ℂ)` of
  $\mathbb{C}^3$.
* A plane curve of degree $d$ is a nonzero homogeneous polynomial $F$ of degree $d$ in the
  homogeneous coordinates $X_0, X_1, X_2$; it need not be reduced or irreducible.
* The curve $F = 0$ passes through $p$ with multiplicity (at least) $m$ iff $F$ lies in the $m$-th
  power of the homogeneous ideal `pointIdeal p` of $p$, which is generated by the linear forms
  vanishing at $p$. In affine coordinates centred at $p$ this says that $F$ has no terms of
  degree $< m$, the usual definition of the multiplicity of a curve at a point.
* "Very general" has its standard meaning: the property holds for all $r$-tuples of points
  outside a countable union of proper Zariski closed subsets of $(\mathbb{P}^2)^r$. Since
  $\mathbb{C}$ is uncountable, such tuples exist.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia: Nagata's conjecture on curves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagata%27s_conjecture_on_curves)
* [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [Nag59] M. Nagata, *On the 14-th problem of Hilbert*, Amer. J. Math. 81 (1959), 766–772.
* [Har01] B. Harbourne, *On Nagata's conjecture*, J. Algebra 236 (2001), 692–702,
  [arXiv:math/9909093](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9909093)
-/
namespace NagatasConjectureOnCurves
open MvPolynomial
open scoped LinearAlgebra.Projectivization
variable {K : Type*} [Field K]

blocks.code:
def pointIdeal (p : ℙ K (Fin 3 → K)) : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin 3) K) :=
  Ideal.span {L | L.IsHomogeneous 1 ∧ eval p.rep L = 0}
blocks.docstring:
The homogeneous ideal of a point `p ∈ ℙ²` in the homogeneous coordinate ring
`K[X₀, X₁, X₂]`: the ideal generated by the linear forms vanishing at `p`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: MvPolynomial.vanishingIdeal (affine sets only, needs an Algebra tower and does not give the homogeneous point ideal directly); Polynomial.rootMultiplicity (univariate only); HomogeneousIdeal / ProjectiveSpectrum (scheme-theoretic, not attached to points of Projectivization).
justification.name: NagatasConjectureOnCurves.pointIdeal
justification.why_needed: The homogeneous ideal of a point of ℙ² (ideal generated by the linear forms vanishing at it); its m-th power encodes 'multiplicity at least m'. Mathlib has no multiplicity/order of vanishing for multivariate polynomials at a point and no ideal of a projective point.

blocks.name: pointIdeal

blocks.docstring:
A polynomial `F ∈ K[X₀, X₁, X₂]` has *multiplicity at least `m`* at a point `p ∈ ℙ²`
if `F` lies in the `m`-th power of the homogeneous ideal of `p`. For a nonzero homogeneous
`F`, this says that the plane curve `F = 0` passes through `p` with multiplicity at least `m`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Polynomial.rootMultiplicity (one variable only), MvPolynomial.pderiv (iterated derivatives; characteristic-dependent and cumbersome), Ideal powers of MvPolynomial.vanishingIdeal of a single affine point (equivalent for homogeneous F, but less standard for projective points).
justification.name: NagatasConjectureOnCurves.HasMultiplicityAtLeast
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of the multiplicity (order of vanishing) of a plane curve / polynomial at a point; defined as F ∈ I(p)^m.

blocks.name: HasMultiplicityAtLeast
blocks.text:
/-- A polynomial `F ∈ K[X₀, X₁, X₂]` has *multiplicity at least `m`* at a point `p ∈ ℙ²`
if `F` lies in the `m`-th power of the homogeneous ideal of `p`. For a nonzero homogeneous
`F`, this says that the plane curve `F = 0` passes through `p` with multiplicity at least `m`. -/
def HasMultiplicityAtLeast (F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) K) (p : ℙ K (Fin 3 → K)) (m : ℕ) :
    Prop :=
  F ∈ pointIdeal p ^ m

blocks.docstring:
A subset of `(ℙ²)^r` is Zariski closed if it is the common zero locus of a family of
polynomials in the `3r` homogeneous coordinates `X i j` (`i : Fin r`, `j : Fin 3`), each of which
is homogeneous separately in each of the `r` blocks of variables `X i 0, X i 1, X i 2`.
Such a zero locus does not depend on the choice of homogeneous coordinates of the points.

justification.closest_existing_considered: MvPolynomial.zeroLocus (affine, Set (σ → K), not projective and not scale-invariant); PrimeSpectrum.zariskiTopology / ProjectiveSpectrum topology (spectra of rings, not sets of K-points of Projectivization).
justification.name: NagatasConjectureOnCurves.IsZariskiClosed
justification.why_needed: Zariski-closed subsets of (ℙ²)^r = (Fin r → ℙ K (Fin 3 → K)), defined as zero loci of families of multi-homogeneous polynomials in the 3r homogeneous coordinates; needed to express 'very general'. Mathlib has no Zariski topology on Projectivization or on tuples of projective points.

blocks.name: IsZariskiClosed
blocks.text:
/-- A subset of `(ℙ²)^r` is Zariski closed if it is the common zero locus of a family of
polynomials in the `3r` homogeneous coordinates `X i j` (`i : Fin r`, `j : Fin 3`), each of which
is homogeneous separately in each of the `r` blocks of variables `X i 0, X i 1, X i 2`.
Such a zero locus does not depend on the choice of homogeneous coordinates of the points. -/
def IsZariskiClosed {r : ℕ} (Z : Set (Fin r → ℙ K (Fin 3 → K))) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Set (MvPolynomial (Fin r × Fin 3) K),
    (∀ F ∈ S, ∃ d : Fin r → ℕ, F.IsWeightedHomogeneous (fun ij => Pi.single ij.1 1) d) ∧
    Z = {p | ∀ F ∈ S, eval (fun ij => (p ij.1).rep ij.2) F = 0}

blocks.docstring:
A property `P` of `r`-tuples of points of `ℙ²` holds for *very general* points if it holds
for all tuples outside a countable union of proper Zariski closed subsets of `(ℙ²)^r`.
(Finite unions are covered by padding the family with the proper closed set `∅`.)

justification.closest_existing_considered: Filter.Eventually / residual sets (topological, would require a topology instance on (ℙ²)^r which does not exist); AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme generic points (scheme-theoretic, not about tuples of closed points).
justification.name: NagatasConjectureOnCurves.ForVeryGeneral
justification.why_needed: The standard 'for very general points' quantifier: a property holds outside a countable union of proper Zariski-closed subsets of (ℙ²)^r. No such notion exists in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib.

blocks.name: ForVeryGeneral
blocks.text:
/-- A property `P` of `r`-tuples of points of `ℙ²` holds for *very general* points if it holds
for all tuples outside a countable union of proper Zariski closed subsets of `(ℙ²)^r`.
(Finite unions are covered by padding the family with the proper closed set `∅`.) -/
def ForVeryGeneral {r : ℕ} (P : (Fin r → ℙ K (Fin 3 → K)) → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ Z : ℕ → Set (Fin r → ℙ K (Fin 3 → K)),
    (∀ n, IsZariskiClosed (Z n) ∧ Z n ≠ Set.univ) ∧ ∀ p ∉ ⋃ n, Z n, P p

@[category research open, AMS 14]
theorem nagatas_conjecture_on_curves (r : ℕ) (hr : 9 < r) (m : Fin r → ℕ)
    (hm : ∀ i, 0 < m i) :
    ForVeryGeneral fun p : Fin r → ℙ ℂ (Fin 3 → ℂ) =>
      ∀ (d : ℕ) (F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℂ), F ≠ 0 → F.IsHomogeneous d →
        (∀ i, HasMultiplicityAtLeast F (p i) (m i)) → (∑ i, (m i : ℝ)) / √r < d := by
  sorry

**Nagata's conjecture on curves.** Suppose $p_1, \dots, p_r$ are very general points in
$\mathbb{P}^2$ and $m_1, \dots, m_r$ are given positive integers. Then for $r > 9$ any curve $C$ in
$\mathbb{P}^2$ that passes through each of the points $p_i$ with multiplicity $m_i$ must satisfy

Here a curve of degree $d$ is a nonzero homogeneous polynomial $F$ of degree $d$ (not necessarily
reduced or irreducible), and "with multiplicity $m_i$" means with multiplicity at least $m_i$,
i.e. $F \in I(p_i)^{m_i}$ where $I(p_i)$ is the homogeneous ideal of $p_i$.

@[category research open, AMS 14]
theorem nagatas_conjecture_on_curves.variants.exists_points (r : ℕ) (hr : 9 < r)
    (m : Fin r → ℕ) (hm : ∀ i, 0 < m i) (d : ℕ)
    (hd : (d : ℝ) ≤ (∑ i, (m i : ℝ)) / √r) :
    ∃ p : Fin r → ℙ ℂ (Fin 3 → ℂ), Function.Injective p ∧
      ∀ F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℂ, F ≠ 0 → F.IsHomogeneous d →
        ¬ ∀ i, HasMultiplicityAtLeast F (p i) (m i) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
An equivalent formulation of Nagata's conjecture avoiding the "very general" quantifier:
for all $r > 9$, positive integers $m_1, \dots, m_r$ and every degree
$d \le \frac{1}{\sqrt r} \sum_i m_i$, there are $r$ distinct points $p_1, \dots, p_r$ of
$\mathbb{P}^2$ such that no curve of degree $d$ passes through each $p_i$ with multiplicity at
least $m_i$.

For fixed $d$ and $m_1, \dots, m_r$, the existence of such a curve is a Zariski closed condition
on $(p_1, \dots, p_r) \in (\mathbb{P}^2)^r$, so it fails for very general points iff it fails for
some tuple of points. This is the form in which the conjecture is stated in [Har01].
blocks.name: nagatas_conjecture_on_curves.variants.exists_points
blocks.text:
/-- An equivalent formulation of Nagata's conjecture avoiding the "very general" quantifier:
for all $r > 9$, positive integers $m_1, \dots, m_r$ and every degree
$d \le \frac{1}{\sqrt r} \sum_i m_i$, there are $r$ distinct points $p_1, \dots, p_r$ of
$\mathbb{P}^2$ such that no curve of degree $d$ passes through each $p_i$ with multiplicity at
least $m_i$.

For fixed $d$ and $m_1, \dots, m_r$, the existence of such a curve is a Zariski closed condition
on $(p_1, \dots, p_r) \in (\mathbb{P}^2)^r$, so it fails for very general points iff it fails for
some tuple of points. This is the form in which the conjecture is stated in [Har01]. -/
@[category research open, AMS 14]
theorem nagatas_conjecture_on_curves.variants.exists_points (r : ℕ) (hr : 9 < r)
    (m : Fin r → ℕ) (hm : ∀ i, 0 < m i) (d : ℕ)
    (hd : (d : ℝ) ≤ (∑ i, (m i : ℝ)) / √r) :
    ∃ p : Fin r → ℙ ℂ (Fin 3 → ℂ), Function.Injective p ∧
      ∀ F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℂ, F ≠ 0 → F.IsHomogeneous d →
        ¬ ∀ i, HasMultiplicityAtLeast F (p i) (m i) := by
  sorry

@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem pointIdeal_ne_top (p : ℙ K (Fin 3 → K)) : pointIdeal p ≠ ⊤ := by
  intro h
  have hle : pointIdeal p ≤ RingHom.ker (eval p.rep) :=
    Ideal.span_le.mpr fun L hL => hL.2
  have h1 : (1 : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) K) ∈ RingHom.ker (eval p.rep) :=
    hle (h ▸ Submodule.mem_top)
  simp at h1
blocks.docstring:
The homogeneous ideal of a point is a proper ideal: a nonzero constant polynomial does not
define a curve passing through `p`.

@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem X_zero_mem_pointIdeal :
    X 0 ∈ pointIdeal (Projectivization.mk K (![0, 0, 1] : Fin 3 → K) (by simp)) := by
  refine Ideal.subset_span ⟨isHomogeneous_X K 0, ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := (Projectivization.mk_eq_mk_iff K _ _ _ _).mp
    (Projectivization.mk_rep (Projectivization.mk K (![0, 0, 1] : Fin 3 → K) (by simp)))
  rw [← ha]
  simp
blocks.docstring: The line `X₀ = 0` passes through the point `[0 : 0 : 1]`.

@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem HasMultiplicityAtLeast.mono {F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) K} {p : ℙ K (Fin 3 → K)}
    {m n : ℕ} (hmn : m ≤ n) (h : HasMultiplicityAtLeast F p n) : HasMultiplicityAtLeast F p m :=
  Ideal.pow_le_pow_right hmn h
blocks.docstring: Multiplicity at least `n` implies multiplicity at least `m` for `m ≤ n`.

  Ideal.pow_le_pow_right hmn h

@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem ForVeryGeneral.of_forall {r : ℕ} {P : (Fin r → ℙ K (Fin 3 → K)) → Prop}
    (h : ∀ p, P p) : ForVeryGeneral P :=
  ⟨fun _ => ∅, fun _ => ⟨isZariskiClosed_empty, Set.empty_ne_univ⟩, fun p _ => h p⟩
blocks.docstring: A property that holds everywhere holds for very general points.

claims.decomposer_note: The list entry only names the conjecture; the precise Prop (from the article / Nagata 1959 / Harbourne math/9909093) is: over an algebraically closed field (take ℂ or any uncountable one so that 'very general' points exist), for every r > 9, every choice of positive integers m_1,…,m_r, and very general points p_1,…,p_r ∈ ℙ² (i.e. outside a countable union of proper Zariski-closed subsets of (ℙ²)^r), every plane curve C (any nonzero homogeneous polynomial, not necessarily reduced or irreducible) with multiplicity AT LEAST m_i at each p_i satisfies the STRICT inequality deg C · √r > Σ m_i; the hypothesis r > 9 is essential (fails for r = 9, e.g. a cubic through 9 points), 'minimal degree' in the entry just describes the conjecture's subject (a lower bound on degree) and is not a separate 'determine d(m,n)' question, and by semicontinuity the 'very general' quantifier may equivalently be formalized as: for all r > 9, m, and d with d·√r ≤ Σ m_i there EXISTS a configuration of r distinct points admitting no degree-d curve with multiplicity ≥ m_i at each p_i (the article notes only the perfect-square case r = s² is known, proved by Nagata — status, not a separately posed question).
claims.reviewer_why: c05's literal 'very general' formulation over ℂ is the most faithful to the Wikipedia statement and its bespoke definitions are exactly right: `pointIdeal p` = span of linear forms vanishing at p (the homogeneous ideal I(p), exact over any field), `IsZariskiClosed` = common zero locus of multihomogeneous polynomials in the 3r homogeneous coordinates (textbook definition, independent of representatives), `ForVeryGeneral` = complement of a countable union of proper closed sets. Main theorem: ∀ r > 9, ∀ m > 0, for very general p, every nonzero homogeneous F of degree d with F ∈ I(p_i)^{m_i} for all i satisfies (Σ m_i)/√r < d (strict). I kept c05's main theorem and its existential variant (Harbourne's form, sanctioned as equivalent by the notes), added a named `HasMultiplicityAtLeast` wrapper (from c01/c06) for readability, and added the API/test lemmas from c01/c05. Line lengths tidied. Verified: F homogeneous ∧ F ∈ I(p)^m ⟺ vanishing to order ≥ m at p; the equivalence very-general ⟺ existential over ℂ holds since the bad locus for fixed (d, m) is Zariski closed (rank condition) and (ℙ²_ℂ)^r is not a countable union of proper closed subsets.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Nagata's conjecture on curves

Nagata's conjecture on curves governs the minimal degree required for a plane algebraic curve to
pass through a collection of very general points with prescribed multiplicities.

**Nagata's conjecture.** Suppose $p_1, \dots, p_r$ are very general points in $\mathbb{P}^2$ and
$m_1, \dots, m_r$ are given positive integers. Then for $r > 9$ any curve $C$ in $\mathbb{P}^2$
that passes through each of the points $p_i$ with multiplicity $m_i$ must satisfy
$$\deg C > \frac{1}{\sqrt r} \sum_{i=1}^r m_i.$$

The condition $r > 9$ is necessary: for $r = 9$ a cubic through nine points has
$\deg C = 3 = \frac{1}{\sqrt 9} \sum_{i=1}^9 1$. The only known case is when $r$ is a perfect
square, which was proved by Nagata [Nag59].

## Formalisation choices

* We work over $\mathbb{C}$, and $\mathbb{P}^2$ is the projectivization `ℙ ℂ (Fin 3 → ℂ)` of
  $\mathbb{C}^3$.
* A plane curve of degree $d$ is a nonzero homogeneous polynomial $F$ of degree $d$ in the
  homogeneous coordinates $X_0, X_1, X_2$; it need not be reduced or irreducible.
* The curve $F = 0$ passes through $p$ with multiplicity (at least) $m$ iff $F$ lies in the $m$-th
  power of the homogeneous ideal `pointIdeal p` of $p$, which is generated by the linear forms
  vanishing at $p$. In affine coordinates centred at $p$ this says that $F$ has no terms of
  degree $< m$, the usual definition of the multiplicity of a curve at a point.
* "Very general" has its standard meaning: the property holds for all $r$-tuples of points
  outside a countable union of proper Zariski closed subsets of $(\mathbb{P}^2)^r$. Since
  $\mathbb{C}$ is uncountable, such tuples exist.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia: Nagata's conjecture on curves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagata%27s_conjecture_on_curves)

namespace NagatasConjectureOnCurves

open MvPolynomial
open scoped LinearAlgebra.Projectivization

variable {K : Type*} [Field K]

/-- The homogeneous ideal of a point `p ∈ ℙ²` in the homogeneous coordinate ring
`K[X₀, X₁, X₂]`: the ideal generated by the linear forms vanishing at `p`. -/
def pointIdeal (p : ℙ K (Fin 3 → K)) : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin 3) K) :=
  Ideal.span {L | L.IsHomogeneous 1 ∧ eval p.rep L = 0}

/-- A polynomial `F ∈ K[X₀, X₁, X₂]` has *multiplicity at least `m`* at a point `p ∈ ℙ²`
if `F` lies in the `m`-th power of the homogeneous ideal of `p`. For a nonzero homogeneous
`F`, this says that the plane curve `F = 0` passes through `p` with multiplicity at least `m`. -/
def HasMultiplicityAtLeast (F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) K) (p : ℙ K (Fin 3 → K)) (m : ℕ) :
    Prop :=
  F ∈ pointIdeal p ^ m

/-- A subset of `(ℙ²)^r` is Zariski closed if it is the common zero locus of a family of
polynomials in the `3r` homogeneous coordinates `X i j` (`i : Fin r`, `j : Fin 3`), each of which
is homogeneous separately in each of the `r` blocks of variables `X i 0, X i 1, X i 2`.
Such a zero locus does not depend on the choice of homogeneous coordinates of the points. -/
def IsZariskiClosed {r : ℕ} (Z : Set (Fin r → ℙ K (Fin 3 → K))) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Set (MvPolynomial (Fin r × Fin 3) K),
    (∀ F ∈ S, ∃ d : Fin r → ℕ, F.IsWeightedHomogeneous (fun ij => Pi.single ij.1 1) d) ∧
    Z = {p | ∀ F ∈ S, eval (fun ij => (p ij.1).rep ij.2) F = 0}

/-- A property `P` of `r`-tuples of points of `ℙ²` holds for *very general* points if it holds
for all tuples outside a countable union of proper Zariski closed subsets of `(ℙ²)^r`.
(Finite unions are covered by padding the family with the proper closed set `∅`.) -/
def ForVeryGeneral {r : ℕ} (P : (Fin r → ℙ K (Fin 3 → K)) → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ Z : ℕ → Set (Fin r → ℙ K (Fin 3 → K)),
    (∀ n, IsZariskiClosed (Z n) ∧ Z n ≠ Set.univ) ∧ ∀ p ∉ ⋃ n, Z n, P p

/-- **Nagata's conjecture on curves.** Suppose $p_1, \dots, p_r$ are very general points in
$\mathbb{P}^2$ and $m_1, \dots, m_r$ are given positive integers. Then for $r > 9$ any curve $C$ in
$\mathbb{P}^2$ that passes through each of the points $p_i$ with multiplicity $m_i$ must satisfy
$$\deg C > \frac{1}{\sqrt r} \sum_{i=1}^r m_i.$$

Here a curve of degree $d$ is a nonzero homogeneous polynomial $F$ of degree $d$ (not necessarily
reduced or irreducible), and "with multiplicity $m_i$" means with multiplicity at least $m_i$,
i.e. $F \in I(p_i)^{m_i}$ where $I(p_i)$ is the homogeneous ideal of $p_i$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 14]
theorem nagatas_conjecture_on_curves (r : ℕ) (hr : 9 < r) (m : Fin r → ℕ)
    (hm : ∀ i, 0 < m i) :
    ForVeryGeneral fun p : Fin r → ℙ ℂ (Fin 3 → ℂ) =>
      ∀ (d : ℕ) (F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℂ), F ≠ 0 → F.IsHomogeneous d →
        (∀ i, HasMultiplicityAtLeast F (p i) (m i)) → (∑ i, (m i : ℝ)) / √r < d := by
  sorry

/-- An equivalent formulation of Nagata's conjecture avoiding the "very general" quantifier:
for all $r > 9$, positive integers $m_1, \dots, m_r$ and every degree
$d \le \frac{1}{\sqrt r} \sum_i m_i$, there are $r$ distinct points $p_1, \dots, p_r$ of
$\mathbb{P}^2$ such that no curve of degree $d$ passes through each $p_i$ with multiplicity at
least $m_i$.

For fixed $d$ and $m_1, \dots, m_r$, the existence of such a curve is a Zariski closed condition
on $(p_1, \dots, p_r) \in (\mathbb{P}^2)^r$, so it fails for very general points iff it fails for
some tuple of points. This is the form in which the conjecture is stated in [Har01]. -/
@[category research open, AMS 14]
theorem nagatas_conjecture_on_curves.variants.exists_points (r : ℕ) (hr : 9 < r)
    (m : Fin r → ℕ) (hm : ∀ i, 0 < m i) (d : ℕ)
    (hd : (d : ℝ) ≤ (∑ i, (m i : ℝ)) / √r) :
    ∃ p : Fin r → ℙ ℂ (Fin 3 → ℂ), Function.Injective p ∧
      ∀ F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℂ, F ≠ 0 → F.IsHomogeneous d →
        ¬ ∀ i, HasMultiplicityAtLeast F (p i) (m i) := by
  sorry

section Tests

/-- The homogeneous ideal of a point is a proper ideal: a nonzero constant polynomial does not
define a curve passing through `p`. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem pointIdeal_ne_top (p : ℙ K (Fin 3 → K)) : pointIdeal p ≠ ⊤ := by
  intro h
  have hle : pointIdeal p ≤ RingHom.ker (eval p.rep) :=
    Ideal.span_le.mpr fun L hL => hL.2
  have h1 : (1 : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) K) ∈ RingHom.ker (eval p.rep) :=
    hle (h ▸ Submodule.mem_top)
  simp at h1

/-- The line `X₀ = 0` passes through the point `[0 : 0 : 1]`. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem X_zero_mem_pointIdeal :
    X 0 ∈ pointIdeal (Projectivization.mk K (![0, 0, 1] : Fin 3 → K) (by simp)) := by
  refine Ideal.subset_span ⟨isHomogeneous_X K 0, ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := (Projectivization.mk_eq_mk_iff K _ _ _ _).mp
    (Projectivization.mk_rep (Projectivization.mk K (![0, 0, 1] : Fin 3 → K) (by simp)))
  rw [← ha]
  simp

/-- Every polynomial has multiplicity at least `0` at every point. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem hasMultiplicityAtLeast_zero (F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) K) (p : ℙ K (Fin 3 → K)) :
    HasMultiplicityAtLeast F p 0 := by
  simp [HasMultiplicityAtLeast]

/-- Multiplicity at least `n` implies multiplicity at least `m` for `m ≤ n`. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem HasMultiplicityAtLeast.mono {F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) K} {p : ℙ K (Fin 3 → K)}
    {m n : ℕ} (hmn : m ≤ n) (h : HasMultiplicityAtLeast F p n) : HasMultiplicityAtLeast F p m :=
  Ideal.pow_le_pow_right hmn h

/-- The whole space `(ℙ²)^r` is Zariski closed. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem isZariskiClosed_univ {r : ℕ} :
    IsZariskiClosed (Set.univ : Set (Fin r → ℙ K (Fin 3 → K))) :=
  ⟨∅, by simp, by simp⟩

/-- The empty subset of `(ℙ²)^r` is Zariski closed. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem isZariskiClosed_empty {r : ℕ} :
    IsZariskiClosed (∅ : Set (Fin r → ℙ K (Fin 3 → K))) :=
  ⟨{1}, fun F hF => ⟨0, by simp_all [isWeightedHomogeneous_one]⟩, by simp⟩

/-- A property that holds everywhere holds for very general points. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem ForVeryGeneral.of_forall {r : ℕ} {P : (Fin r → ℙ K (Fin 3 → K)) → Prop}
    (h : ∀ p, P p) : ForVeryGeneral P :=
  ⟨fun _ => ∅, fun _ => ⟨isZariskiClosed_empty, Set.empty_ne_univ⟩, fun p _ => h p⟩

end Tests

end NagatasConjectureOnCurves

items: Base field: ℂ (the canonical setting for 'very general points in ℙ²'; ℂ is uncountable so the complement of a countable union of proper closed subsets is nonempty and the statement is non-vacuous). Definitions are stated over an arbitrary field K, theorems over ℂ.

ℙ² is Mathlib's `Projectivization ℂ (Fin 3 → ℂ)`; a plane curve of degree d is a nonzero `MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℂ` that is `IsHomogeneous d` (not required to be reduced or irreducible; `F ≠ 0 ∧ IsHomogeneous d` forces degree exactly d).

'Passes through p_i with multiplicity m_i' is read as multiplicity AT LEAST m_i (standard in the fat-points literature and equivalent for the conjecture), encoded as F ∈ (pointIdeal p)^m where pointIdeal p is the ideal generated by the linear forms vanishing at p. For p = [0:0:1] this is (X₀,X₁)^m, i.e. the dehomogenised F has no terms of degree < m, the usual multiplicity; the general case follows by a linear change of coordinates. This characterisation is valid in every characteristic (unlike a partial-derivative definition).

'Very general' is formalised literally: ∃ Z : ℕ → Set ((ℙ²)^r) with each Z n Zariski closed and ≠ univ, such that the conclusion holds for all p ∉ ⋃ n, Z n. Zariski-closed subsets of (ℙ²)^r are defined as common zero loci of families of polynomials in the 3r homogeneous coordinates that are homogeneous in each block of 3 variables (encoded via `IsWeightedHomogeneous (fun ij => Pi.single ij.1 1) F d`); such loci are independent of the chosen representatives `Projectivization.rep`. Finite families are covered by padding with ∅ (proper and closed).
The inequality is written literally as (∑ i, (m i : ℝ)) / √r < d, matching deg C > (1/√r) Σ m_i; r > 9 makes √r > 0 so division is genuine.
The countable family of bad closed sets may depend on r and m (quantifier order: ∀ r m, ∃ Z, ∀ p); since there are countably many (r, m) this is equivalent to a uniform choice.

Included variant `nagatas_conjecture_on_curves.variants.exists_points` (research open): for every d ≤ (Σ m_i)/√r there exist r distinct points admitting no degree-d curve with multiplicity ≥ m_i at each p_i. Equivalent to the main statement because the existence of such a curve is a Zariski-closed condition on the point configuration (semicontinuity) and (ℙ²_ℂ)^r is not a countable union of proper closed subsets.

Included variant `nagatas_conjecture_on_curves.variants.square` (research solved): the same statement under the extra hypothesis `IsSquare r`, proved by Nagata (1959) as recorded in the article's 'Current status'.
Added `category test` lemmas for the bespoke definitions: pointIdeal_ne_top, X_zero_mem_pointIdeal (the line X₀ = 0 passes through [0:0:1]), isZariskiClosed_univ, isZariskiClosed_empty.

reviewer_notes: All eight candidates compile and all state a mathematically correct version of the conjecture; none was unfaithful in a way that changes the claim. Differences: c01/c03/c05 use the literal 'very general' quantifier (c01's and c03's Zariski-closed notions rely on k infinite to coincide with the standard one — fine over ℂ but less transparent than c05's multihomogeneous definition; c03's multiplicity via the affine maximal ideal 𝔪_v^m is correct only because F is homogeneous). c06/c07/c08 use the existential (semicontinuity) form over ℙ² — c07/c08 with no bespoke definitions (c08's kernel of X_j ↦ p_j T is exactly I(p); c07's 𝔪_rep^m is correct for homogeneous F). c06 states it over an arbitrary algebraically closed field (Harbourne's setting) rather than ℂ; not wrong, but I kept ℂ as the safest reading of the Wikipedia statement. c02/c04 work in an affine chart with totalDegree ≤ d — equivalent by homogenization but least literal. I omitted the 'research solved' perfect-square variants (c05, c06) since they are not part of the adjudicated slot and Nagata's exact theorem (uniform vs. non-uniform multiplicities) is a status remark, not a posed question. Ambiguities in the original: 'multiplicity m_i' is read as 'at least m_i'; curves are arbitrary nonzero homogeneous forms (not necessarily reduced/irreducible); the countable family of bad closed sets is allowed to depend on r and m (equivalent to a uniform family, since there are countably many m). The final file was also built in place as FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/NagatasConjectureOnCurves.lean with `lake --wfail build` (all repository linters pass) and then removed.
statement: Nagata's conjecture on curves, specifically the minimal degree required for a plane algebraic curve to pass through a collection of very general points with prescribed multiplicities.
